handshake.instructions:
This agent scans BSC lending and liquidity protocols (Venus,
PancakeSwap), scores each opportunity by risk-adjusted yield rather than raw
APR, and migrates capital when the improvement exceeds gas, swap, slippage and a
safety margin.

Every tool here is read-only, except `pause`, which is an emergency stop. You
CANNOT execute a migration through this interface — `simulate_rebalance` shows
what the agent would do, and only a human can make it do it.

The capital under management is the AGENT'S OWN. It custodies nothing on anyone
else's behalf, so a position reported here belongs to the agent's wallet.

Useful order: `get_status` for the current picture, `scan_protocols` for fresh
data (~20s), `simulate_rebalance` to see the decision and its reasoning.

declared.name: get_status
declared.description: Current state: capital, held position, best opportunity, last scan.

declared.name: get_metadata
declared.description: What this agent is, which protocols it supports, and its on-chain identity.

declared.name: get_strategy
declared.description: The declared strategy and the risk controls currently in force.

declared.name: get_opportunities
declared.description:
Opportunities from the LAST scan, with risk scores. Does not re-scan —
    use ``scan_protocols`` for fresh data.

declared.name: get_positions
declared.description:
What the agent currently holds. This is the AGENT'S OWN capital — it
    custodies nothing on anyone else's behalf.

declared.name: get_performance
declared.description: Migration counts and cumulative gas, derived from the audit log.

declared.name: get_transactions
declared.description: The audit trail (spec section 13), newest first.

declared.name: get_chain_info
declared.description: Network, block height, gas price and the native token price.

declared.name: scan_protocols
declared.description:
Read Venus and PancakeSwap live and re-score every opportunity.

    Reads chain and subgraph state; changes no position and signs nothing.
    Takes roughly 20 seconds.

    REQUIRES AN API KEY — twenty seconds of RPC per call is a denial-of-service
    vector if left open, and the results are readable afterwards through the
    unauthenticated `get_opportunities`.

declared.name: simulate_rebalance
declared.description:
Evaluate the migration rule and return the decision WITHOUT executing.

    Equivalent to ``POST /rebalance?dry_run=true``. This is the closest a model
    can get to migrating: it can ask what the agent WOULD do, never make it do
    it.

    REQUIRES AN API KEY — it scans if the data is stale and then makes an LLM
    call, so it costs both time and money per invocation.

declared.name: pause
declared.description:
Emergency stop. Refuses all further migrations; scanning continues.

    The only state-changing tool exposed, because it fails SAFE — the worst a
    hostile prompt achieves is halting an agent that was about to trade. There
    is deliberately no matching ``activate`` tool: resuming trading is a
    decision for a human, not for a model reading untrusted text.

    REQUIRES AN API KEY. Failing safe is a reason to expose it at all, not a
    reason to leave it open to anyone who finds the URL.
